title: Activation of Physical Pocketwire Visa Debit Cards
content:
**Cardholder terms: activation.**

**(a) Who activates.** The customer activates a physical Pocketwire Visa Debit Card in the app, using the card's last four digits and security code. A support representative cannot activate a card for the customer. Virtual cards are activated when they are issued.

**(b) Closure of a card never activated.** A physical card that is still ordered and has never been activated is closed by the system once its activation window has passed. The closure is recorded later than the tier's activation window, in calendar days, after the card's issue date.

**(c) Counting the window.** The activation window is counted in calendar days from the card's issue date. The day after issue is day 1. The card can still be activated on the last day of the window.

**(d) Replacement cards.** Activating a replacement card closes the card it replaces on the same day.

### How the window is judged

- *Clock starts:* the card's issue date, as recorded on the card.
- *Evidence:* the company's record of the card, meaning its issue date and its status (still ordered). A customer's statement about when the card arrived does not move the start date.
- *Comparison:* a closure can be recorded only on a day that is later than the last day of the window. The last day itself is still inside the window.

### Boundary illustration (hypothetical dates, 60-day window)

A card is issued on 1 March. 2 March is day 1, and 30 April is day 60.

| Date | Day of window | Can the customer still activate? | Can the system record the closure? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 April | day 60, the last day | yes | no |
| 1 May | day 61 | the card is past its window | yes, since this is later than 60 days after issue |

On a 90-day tier the same count runs to day 90. The closure can be recorded from day 91.
